haiku-low.q1: No. Cursors never touch the document service or Postgres. They are stored and published only in Redis.
haiku-low.q2: Clients send at most one cursor per 50 ms, with a trailing timer. The node silently drops any cursor less than 50 ms after the last accepted one from that connection.
haiku-low.q3: It holds the caret and draws it once appliedRev reaches that rev.
haiku-low.q4: If rev is at or below appliedRev, it maps the position forward with transformPosition. If history is gone (HistoryGone), the caret is dropped until the next update.
haiku-low.q5: Shown per user, not per tab. A user stays listed while any of their connections is live. They disappear when their last connection closes or its entries go stale.
haiku-low.q6: After a clean tab close, within 2 s. After the gateway node dies, within 35 s of the crash.
haiku-low.q7: Redis: presence:doc sorted set (member per connection, score = last heartbeat) and cursors:doc hash (field = connId). Heartbeats every 10 s refresh them; keys have 60 s TTL.
haiku-low.q8: Surviving nodes' 5 s sweeps remove members older than 30 s and their cursor fields. They send presence_users to their clients only if the user list changed. Sending cursor_gone on sweep is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q9: The accepting node writes the caret to cursors:doc and publishes on cursor:doc. Other nodes forward it to their clients. Delivery to viewers on the sender's own node is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q10: The node subscribes first and holds live frames until the snapshot is sent. Overlap may repeat messages, which the seq rule makes harmless.
haiku-low.q11: Each client sends one cursor right after its open completes, so idle users' carets are stored in cursors:doc and included in the joiner's snapshot.
haiku-low.q12: The receiver keeps the highest seq per connId and discards any message with a lower or equal seq. A held caret is replaced only by a higher seq.

sonnet.q1: No. Cursors never touch the document service or Postgres; they live only in Redis (hash cursors:doc) and pub/sub.
sonnet.q2: At most one cursor per 50 ms per client (with a trailing timer so the last position is sent). The node silently drops any cursor arriving less than 50 ms after the last accepted one from that connection, with no message back.
sonnet.q3: It holds the caret and draws it once its appliedRev reaches that rev (a held caret is replaced only by a higher seq).
sonnet.q4: It is mapped forward with transformPosition(pos, rev, appliedRev), and re-mapped on each applied revision. If history is gone (HistoryGone, beyond the last 500 revisions), the caret is dropped until the next update.
sonnet.q5: Shown once, per user not per tab (distinct userIds among live members). They disappear only when their last connection is gone; closing one of two tabs changes nothing visible.
sonnet.q6: Clean tab close: within 2 s. Node death: at most 35 s after the crash (inside the 45 s limit).
sonnet.q7: In Redis: presence in sorted set presence:doc, one member per connection (score = last heartbeat time), and carets in hash cursors:doc (field = connId). Kept fresh by a 10 s heartbeat (ZADD score and EXPIRE 60 on both keys); stale entries are removed by the 5 s sweep (older than 30 s).
sonnet.q8: The 5 s sweeps on surviving nodes with local sockets on the doc remove members older than 30 s (ZREMRANGEBYSCORE) and HDEL the cursors. Those nodes then send presence_users to their own clients when the user list changed.
sonnet.q9: The node writes it to cursors:doc (HSET) and publishes on Redis channel cursor:doc. Subscribed other nodes receive it and forward a cursor frame to their clients. For a viewer on the sender's own node: NOT STATED (the node is subscribed to cursor:doc too, but the document does not say how same-node delivery works).
sonnet.q10: The node subscribes to presence:doc and cursor:doc first, then writes its member, reads members and the cursor hash, sends presence_snapshot, and only then forwards live frames (held until the snapshot is sent). Overlap may repeat a message, and the seq rule makes repeats harmless.
sonnet.q11: Each client sends one cursor right after its open completes, so idle users have a caret stored in cursors:doc, which is kept while idle. The joiner gets it in the presence_snapshot via HGETALL.
sonnet.q12: The receiver keeps the highest seq per connId and discards any message with lower or equal seq. A held caret is replaced only by a higher seq. The sender's seq only increases.
